title: Signed payload signer: an empty or 65+ byte payload is encoded into a P key that the SDK itself cannot decode

target.versions_affected: 17.0.0 - 17.0.1 (executed: 17.0.0, 17.0.1; main 3d722d01 has the same code; earlier versions not run)

severity_basis: Encode side only: SignerKey.ed25519_signed_payload() and StrKey.encode_ed25519_signed_payload() do not check the payload length, so an empty or 65-byte payload is encoded into a P strkey that the SDK's own decoder refuses. The same gap is public in js-stellar-sdk and go-stellar-sdk and fixed in rs-stellar-strkey.

entries.expected: refuse to encode a signed payload of 0 bytes (SEP-23 and CAP-0040: 1 to 64 bytes)
entries.observed: Executed on 17.0.0 and 17.0.1: StrKey.encode_ed25519_signed_payload emits PA7QYNF7…AAAAAAKH4Y for an empty payload; the SDK's own decoder refuses the text it emitted.

entries.expected: refuse to encode a signed payload of 65 bytes (SEP-23 and CAP-0040: 1 to 64 bytes)
entries.observed: Executed on 17.0.0 and 17.0.1: StrKey.encode_ed25519_signed_payload emits a P strkey for a 65-byte payload; the SDK's own decoder refuses it.

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner, L4, python@17.0.0 and python@17.0.1 (make verify-conformance and make verify-conformance-public), entries strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-empty and strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-65-bytes: accepts_invalid, reason own_output_rejected.
evidence.expected_basis: CAP-40 defines the payload as opaque payload<64> and SetOptionsOp fails with SET_OPTIONS_BAD_SIGNER on an empty one; SEP-23 (https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/f2d364902615af726b3533021403c8b225aa6e5d/ecosystem/sep-0023.md) bounds the strkey accordingly, and the SDK's own decoder requires 40 to 100 bytes of data for this version byte.

reproduction.method: Re-run on 2026-11-18: the 4 listed report rows failed again in make verify-conformance-public and make verify-conformance, offline; the issue's script on 17.0.1 encodes 0 and 65 bytes and refuses to decode both.

history.note: Recorded on 2026-11-18: filed by the maintainers of this kit on 2026-11-14 as https://github.com/StellarCN/py-stellar-base/issues/1256; this record restates the public issue.
Upstream: the maintainer closed the issue on 2026-11-16 as fixed on main by pull request #1265 (the SDK moved to stellar-strkey); no release after 17.0.1 includes it yet.
